beats.text: This is me at two in the morning with forty seven dollars of stuff in my cart that I did not need at ten o'clock.
A neck pillow. A tiny waffle maker. And a lamp shaped like a cat. I don't even like cats.
I woke up the next morning and saw the order confirmation. And I swear I had no memory of buying a cat lamp. It was like a different guy did it.
And every time I tell myself the same thing. You're just bad with money Dave.
But what if that's not true? What if your brain was built for a world that doesn't exist anymore?
By the end of this video you'll know the one trick that makes your old brain save money without using any willpower at all.
But most people scroll away before that part which is exactly the old brain doing its thing.
So let me introduce you to my great great great great great grandpa. Way more greats. Let's call him Grug.
Grug lives in a cave. No fridge. No bank. No tomorrow that he can count on.
One day Grug finds a bush full of berries. And what does Grug do? He eats every single berry. Right now.
And honestly? Smart move Grug. Because if he saves them for later a bear eats them. Or the berries rot. Or Grug gets eaten himself.
There's no berry bank. There's no freezer. Food you don't eat today is food you don't have. So Grug's brain learned one lesson really really well.
Grug's financial plan.
For hundreds of thousands of years the rule was simple. Something good in front of you? Take it now. Later might never come.
The people who waited didn't become our ancestors. The ones who grabbed did. You come from a very long line of grabbers.
Me realizing my whole family tree is just people grabbing berries.
And here's the thing. Grug's brain is the brain you're using right now to watch this video. It got a few updates. But the main code is the same.
It's like running the newest app on a phone from the stone age. It works. Kind of. But it crashes every time somebody says limited offer.
Now take Grug and drop him in a mall. Or worse. Give him a phone with a shopping app at two in the morning.
Every screen is a berry bush now. Shoes. Snacks. Gadgets. All of it shouting take me now. And Grug brain says yes. Every time.
A cave with a berry bush outside was rare. A phone with a million berries in your pocket is every single day. Your brain never had to deal with that much yes.
Grug with free next day delivery.
In Grug's world later was dangerous. In your world later is where all the money is. And your brain didn't get the memo.
So scientists actually put people inside brain scanners and showed them stuff to buy. Chocolates. Gadgets. Things with price tags.
And when people saw something they wanted a pleasure part of the brain lit up. Before they even saw the price.
Then the price showed up. And if it felt too high another part of the brain lit up. The part that feels pain.
Which makes sense. Grug's brain treats losing stuff like losing food. Losing hurts. And if paying hurts enough Grug walks away.
So buying something is a fight inside your head. Pleasure on one side. Pain on the other. And whoever wins decides if you click buy.
My brain at checkout.
And now here's the sneaky part. What if somebody could turn down the pain? Then pleasure wins every single time.
Somebody did. It's called a credit card.
Two professors at MIT once auctioned real basketball tickets. Half the people had to pay cash. The other half could pay with a card.
Same tickets. Same game. The card people offered about twice as much money.
Cash feels like losing something. You watch the bills leave your hand. A card feels like nothing. A little beep. And the pain never shows up.
Have you noticed how easy it is to spend fifty dollars on an app but how hard it is to hand someone a fifty dollar bill? Same fifty dollars. Totally different feeling.
Me paying with cash versus paying with my phone.
And now it's even easier. Tap your phone. Save your card in the app. One click buy. Every step you skip is a little less pain.
Casinos figured this out decades ago. That's why you don't bet with dollars at a casino. You bet with plastic chips. Chips don't feel like money. So you lose more.
Casinos when they invented chips.
It's like taking the brakes out of a car because they slow you down. Technically yes. That's what brakes are for.
And this is where it gets dark. Because companies know all of this. They study it. They hire people whose whole job is to talk to your Grug brain.

Me buying something because a timer told me to.

The shoes I looked at once.

Here's the part that changed how I see myself. The marshmallow test. Kids get one marshmallow now or two if they wait. The story was the kids who waited became more successful.

But when scientists ran it again with way more kids a lot of that difference shrank. It had a lot to do with the kid's home. Kids who grew up unsure there'd be a second marshmallow took the first one.
That's not weakness. That's Grug logic. When tomorrow feels shaky your brain grabs today. And money stress makes tomorrow feel very shaky.
So if you've ever felt like a failure because you can't save. You're not broken. You're running very old software in a world built to hack it.
And here's the thing nobody says. The people telling you to just have more discipline usually have a safety net. When you know there's a second marshmallow waiting is easy.
Me finding out it's not entirely my fault.

And now the big question. If willpower is fighting a million years of instinct how does anyone ever save money?
Here's what I learned. People who save money aren't stronger than you. They just stopped fighting Grug. They went around him. Quick reminder this is education and not advice.
The trick is simple. Make the saving happen before Grug ever sees the money. Automatic. On payday. Without asking you.
Because Grug can only spend what he can see. If the money moves to savings or into an investment the second your paycheck lands Grug never even knows it existed.
Out of sight out of mind. Your savings account is the top shelf. Your checking account is the berry bush right next to the cave.
It's like hiding the cookies on the top shelf. You still could get them. But you'd need a chair. And Grug is lazy.
Me setting up automatic savings once and never thinking about it again.
Two economists tested this with real workers. Instead of asking people to save more now they asked them to save more later. Every time they got a raise a little more went to savings.
Grug said sure. Later sounds easy. Later is not my problem. And years later those workers were saving way more than before. Without feeling any pain.
They used Grug's own weakness against him. He loves now and ignores later. So they put the saving in later. Genius.
Second trick. Put some pain back. Delete your saved card from shopping apps. Now every purchase needs you to go find your wallet. Grug hates walking to the other room.
Third. The twenty four hour rule. Want something that isn't food or rent? Leave it in the cart for a day. Half the time tomorrow me doesn't even remember what it was.
I tried it with a pair of headphones. Day one I needed them. Day two I kind of wanted them. Day three I forgot they existed. Saved a hundred and twenty dollars by doing nothing.
Me after the twenty four hour rule.
My cart after twenty four hours.
And fourth. Turn off the shopping notifications. Every red dot is someone tapping Grug on the shoulder saying hey berries.
And the best part is investing works the same way. If a little money goes into an investment automatically every month Grug can't panic and pull it out every time the news gets scary.
Grug checking his investments every day versus Grug who forgot he even has them.
The less Grug touches it the better it grows. That's the funniest thing about money. Sometimes doing nothing is the smartest move.
Every year I look at it and think wait I did that? No. Grug didn't. The system did. I just set it up once and walked away.
So that's the trick. Don't fight your brain. Build a system so your brain never gets the chance to say yes.
